Your Landscape Plan

Select a zone to review the planting and materials. Tap any plant for details.

Front Yard
No lawn. Layered planting bed.
The driveway and entry stay as-is. A single planting bed runs across the front, grounded in decomposed granite with a clean stone edge.
One dwarf lemon tree
Improved Meyer Lemon, semi-dwarf. Small enough for the fire zone. White blossoms in winter, fruit nearly year-round.
Entry lions and planters stay
Cement lions remain on whitewashed brick pedestals. Pottery Barn planters with seasonal faux trees — the covered entry doesn't get enough sun for live planting.
Existing hedges kept
Ballerina Indian Hawthorn along the property line. Existing Podocarpus at 12 ft stays intact.

Side Yards
Simple. Reuse what's there.
Existing interlocking blocks are on-site from prior foundation work. They get reused to re-form the terraced levels — no new material needed unless quantities fall short.
Existing retaining blocks reused
Set aside during foundation work. Back on site, ready to reuse. Pavestone Limestone blocks from Home Depot fill any gaps.
24-inch step stones
Pavestone Granite Blend set in pea gravel. A simple walkway between the terraced levels.
Drainage swale — contractor to confirm
A swale along the north property line is likely needed. Flagged here — exact design falls to the landscaper during grading.
New wood fence and gate
50 ft of fixed wood fence plus a new gate. Pea gravel at the gate area. All grades slope away from the foundation.
Standing note: All grades slope away from foundation. Plantings set away from foundation where feasible. Prior water intrusion noted.

Rear Yard
Keep the hedges. Add a lawn and underplanting.
The existing Podocarpus along the patio wall stays — infilled where it didn't make it through the fires. New lawn in the open area. New planting covers the base of the old yellow wall.
Podocarpus — keep and infill
Existing 12-ft hedges along the patio wall stay. New 15-gal columns added where gaps formed. A second screening row goes along the north property line.
Camellia and Foxtail Fern
Camellia 'Nuccio's Gem' — white double blooms in winter, suits diffused light under the eaves. Foxtail Fern alongside for texture and wall coverage.
Shade planting under eaves
Grassland Sedge and Fragrant Sweet Box for the low-sun corners. Shade annuals at the base for seasonal color.
Sunny corner — roses and rosemary
White Iceberg climbing roses along the old fence. Tuscan Blue Rosemary in the same spot. The one part of the rear yard that gets full sun.
